courses.title: WebSocket Communications with Node and Angular
courses.why: Builds a live chat on a TypeScript Node.js WebSocket backend with an Angular front end; you already know Angular, so the time goes into the WebSocket protocol and patterns.

courses.title: gRPC in Python
courses.why: A 41-minute course on protocol buffers, HTTP/2, a gRPC server and client, streaming responses and interceptors: the gRPC half of this path in one sitting.

portals.name: MDN: The WebSocket API
portals.what: The browser WebSocket API reference and guides, including writing your own WebSocket server.

portals.name: MDN: Using server-sent events
portals.what: The event-stream format, EventSource, reconnection and Last-Event-ID, worked through with examples.

portals.name: gRPC: Node.js basics tutorial (official)
portals.what: Write all four kinds of RPC (unary, server, client and bidirectional streaming) in Node.js step by step.

portals.name: gRPC: Python basics tutorial (official)
portals.what: The same route-guide exercise in Python, useful if the backend you interview for is Python.

portals.name: javascript.info: WebSocket
portals.what: A clear walkthrough of the handshake, frames, ping/pong and close codes, with a small chat example.

assessments.name: Rest API (Intermediate) certification
assessments.format: 1 hr 30 min online test, 2 questions on working with APIs; one attempt only
assessments.credential: HackerRank certificate with a shareable URL
assessments.why: There is no recognised certification for WebSockets, SSE or gRPC, so pair an API certificate with the project below, which is the real proof for this path.

assessments.name: Node.js (Intermediate) certification
assessments.format: 1-hour online test, 2 coding questions, one attempt (topics include event-driven architecture)
assessments.credential: HackerRank certificate with a shareable URL
assessments.why: Event-driven server code is the core skill behind real-time backends.
